title: The existing gradient scalars against the signed negative-log-likelihood changes (publication recovery plan, task 1b): protocol fixed before the run
status: POST HOC (selected after D-094). Written before the code and the run. Amendment A9 (the executed gradient baseline), the D-094 and D-095 tables and the original claim rules are unchanged; this adds an analysis of the stored scalars on their own target.
honesty_note: All items had been analysed under the original rules before this protocol was written, and I had looked at the columns of three items of the main INT16 table to check units (mean NLL scale, sign convention: g_pred_fp and dloss_FP_FP are of the same order and sign); no statistic of this analysis was computed or read before this file. No threshold below was chosen from outcomes.
source: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-26-publication-recovery-after-results.md Task 1, bullet 'Re-evaluate existing gradient scalars against existing signed NLL changes and shifts' (Codex); amendment_A9_gradient_scalars.json
question: How well does the first-order loss prediction of the executed A9 baseline (minus the dot product of the autograd gradient of the mean NLL and the edit, summed over the edited rows) match the signed NLL change that the same edit actually produces, in the full-precision model, in the quantized model, and in the quantized-minus-full-precision shift? This is the scalar NLL gradient on a scalar NLL target; the vector-valued first-order logit effect (the logit JVP) was never computed and is not tested here.

comparisons.C0: prediction g_pred_fp against dloss_FP_FP (FP model, FP edit; identical in the three state tables, which is asserted and reported)
comparisons.C1: g_pred_q_fixed against dloss_Q_Q (quantized model and quantized prefix, the fixed FP edit)
comparisons.C2: g_pred_q_native against dloss_Q_Q_native (quantized model, the edit with the quantized state's own amplitude)
comparisons.S1: the shift g_pred_q_fixed - g_pred_fp against dloss_Q_Q - dloss_FP_FP
comparisons.S2: the shift g_pred_q_native - g_pred_fp against dloss_Q_Q_native - dloss_FP_FP

groups: real direction, all items (primary); real direction, eligible items (the eligibility flag of the main tables; the scalar endpoint does not need it, the subset is reported for comparability); the four control directions pooled (secondary); real-direction items in terciles of the FP edit norm (edit_norm_fp, the terciles of the corpus) to show the dependence on the size of the intervention; no extrapolation beyond the actual edit size is claimed
states: INT16 (rounding reference: the shifts there should be near zero, so it is the noise reference of S1 and S2)
statistics: per comparison and group: Pearson correlation r; the through-origin slope beta = sum(p a) / sum(p^2) of the actual change a on the prediction p; the through-origin R2 = 1 - sum((a - beta p)^2) / sum(a^2); the sign agreement (share of items with sign(a) = sign(p)); and the sign agreement among the items whose actual change exceeds the noise threshold |a| > t, t = the 95th percentile of |dloss_Q_Q - dloss_FP_FP| over the real items of the INT16 table of the same corpus (the same t for every state and comparison of that corpus; the INT16 rounding reference). Items with a missing value in either quantity are left out and counted. Intervals: crossed bootstrap over features and source clusters (the external panel: passages), 2,000 replicates, seed 20261026, 95 % percentile, weights = multiplicity of the feature times that of the cluster in every statistic.
reading_rules: No threshold declares the gradient baseline 'good' or 'bad'; the numbers are reported as they are, with the INT16 reference next to INT6 and INT4. A statement that gradient attribution predicts the effect-vector error (the original claim) is not retested; this analysis can only say how well the stored scalars approximate the scalar NLL change.
code: scripts/g0/phase1_transfer_gradient_check.py with scripts/g0/tests_torch/test_phase1_transfer_gradient_check.py (tests first, mutation checked); outputs in reports/intervention_transfer/results/recovery/ (gradient_vs_nll.csv, gradient_vs_nll.json)
